```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="k06" data-src="../assets/learn/data/10-write-it-down.json ../assets/learn/data/town.json ../assets/learn/data/town_year.json ../assets/learn/data/path.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Lesson 10's hour, 19:00, as arrays, in seven moves</p>
<ol>
<li>A plan is a vector, an ordered list: x = (100, 45) is 100 MW from the combined-cycle plant and 45 MW from the peaker; (45, 100) is a different plan.</li>
<li>The cost is a dot product: c · x = 40 × 100 + 100 × 45 = 8,500 dollars for the hour.</li>
<li>The four rules stack into a matrix A, one row per rule and one column per decision.</li>
<li>A x is every row's dot product with x: (145, 100, 45, 61.75), one number per rule.</li>
<li>Multiplying the cover row by −1 turns x + y ≥ 145 into −x − y ≤ −145, so every row reads ≤.</li>
<li>A x ≤ b checks all four rules at once: (150, 100) covers the 145 MW and fits both plants, but emits 110.5 t, so only the CO₂ row fails.</li>
<li>A is 4 × 2 here; lesson 11's day is 72 rows × 96 columns, with only 190 of its 6,912 entries not zero.</li>
</ol>
```

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="k6-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Vector</dt><dd>An ordered list of numbers; the order is the meaning: x = (100, 45).</dd>
<dt>Dot product</dt><dd>Multiply two vectors in pairs and add: c · x = 8,500 dollars.</dd>
<dt>Matrix</dt><dd>A table of numbers with m rows and n columns: here one row per rule, one column per decision.</dd>
<dt>A x</dt><dd>Every row's dot product with x, one number per rule.</dd>
<dt>A x ≤ b</dt><dd>Every rule at once: each entry of A x at most its limit in b.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The form solvers read, and sparse matrices</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Two-sided rows and bounds.** HiGHS, the solver in lessons 11 and B1, reads a model as $\min c^\mathsf{T} x$ with $L \le Ax \le U$ and $l \le x \le u$: rows get a lower and an upper limit, and simple limits on one decision are bounds, not rows. Lesson 10's two size rules would be bounds.
- **The transpose.** $c^\mathsf{T} x$ (B1's notation) is the dot product written as a row times a column; $\mathsf{T}$ turns a column into a row.
- **Sparse.** Large models are mostly zeros: each rule touches a few decisions. Lesson 11's day has 190 non-zero entries out of 6,912, about 2.7%, so solvers store only those.
- **Where next.** Modeler lessons build these arrays in code ([M1](m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html)); Gaussian processes (M9, upcoming) work with matrices of similarities between data points.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="k6-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="order" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “(100, 45) and (45, 100) are the same plan: the same two numbers.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. The order is the meaning: the first costs 8,500 dollars, the second 11,800, because the peaker's MWh cost more.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="flip" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Multiplying a rule by −1 keeps the same plans if the sign flips too.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. x + y ≥ 145 and −x − y ≤ −145 pass exactly the same plans.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="k6">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="ax" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">With A's rows (1, 1) and (0.37, 0.55), what is A x for x = (145, 0)?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">(145, 145)</li><li data-value="b">(145, 53.65)</li><li data-value="c">(145, 79.75)</li><li data-value="d">(0, 53.65)</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>(145, 53.65): 1 × 145 + 1 × 0 = 145 and 0.37 × 145 + 0.55 × 0 = 53.65. (145, 79.75) uses the peaker's rate on the combined-cycle MW.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="shape" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">A model has 3 decisions and 2 rules in each of 24 hours. What size is A?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">2 rows × 3 columns</li><li data-value="b">72 rows × 48 columns</li><li data-value="c">48 rows × 72 columns</li><li data-value="d">24 rows × 24 columns</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>48 rows × 72 columns: one row per rule (2 × 24 = 48) and one column per decision (3 × 24 = 72).</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="k6-drill"></div>
```
